article_content: The Ondo State Government has reluctantly admitted that Governor Rotimi Akeredolu authorized spending N7.3 billion without the mandatory House of Assembly approval. This money, supposedly for 'Contingency', was spent while the governor was on a prolonged medical trip in Germany from July to September. Panic over the unexplained expenditure is quickly spreading, with citizens intensely questioning the transparency of their leaders. While Chief Press Secretary Richard Olatunde continued to reject the allegations, contradictions remain. He asserted, 'Transparency and accountability are values synonymous with the Akeredolu-led administration,' yet the allocation bypassed legislative oversight, calling transparency into question. Olatunde acknowledged, 'The referenced N7.3 billion constituted the cumulative amount of palliative funds received from the Federal Government.' However, these funds were put under the vague heading of 'contingency', leading to challenges in tracing how the funds were actually used and if they truly benefitted the public. He further pointed out, 'The contingency fund in the 2023 budget was N1,069,000,000.00, but the additional N7 billion, referred to as Infrastructure Support Fund, is especially questionable since it was not thoroughly explained to the Assembly or public.' Despite citing the Ondo State Public Finance Management Law 2017 as justification, critics argue that repeating legal references acts more as a diversion than an explanation. Olatunde stated, 'A contingency Fund is hereby established... the contingency fund may be utilised for emergency expenditure... which cannot without serious injury to the public interest be postponed.' Alarm is mounting among citizens as 'contingency' funds lack specific earmarks. Many believe the actual use and beneficiaries of the spending remain hidden. Olatunde says Akeredolu did not personally spend the N7.3 billion and that the funds were for palliatives, but public watchdogs highlight omissions in accessible expenditure reports. Mounting anxiety is fueled by the continued delay in publishing a full breakdown. The palliative committee is yet to deliver the promised detailed report, leaving public trust in serious doubt.
translated_content: รัฐบาลรัฐออนโดยอมรับอย่างไม่เต็มใจว่า ผู้ว่าการโรทิมิ อาเคเรโดลู อนุมัติการใช้จ่ายเงิน 7.3 พันล้านไนรา โดยไม่ได้รับความเห็นชอบจากสภา เงินก้อนนี้ซึ่งอ้างว่าเป็น 'เหตุฉุกเฉิน' ถูกใช้งานในช่วงที่ผู้ว่าการเดินทางไปรักษาตัวที่เยอรมนีระหว่างเดือนกรกฎาคมถึงกันยายน สังคมเกิดกระแสตื่นตระหนกกับรายจ่ายที่อธิบายไม่ได้ ประชาชนเริ่มตั้งคำถามถึงความโปร่งใสของผู้นำมากขึ้น แม้หัวหน้าเลขาธิการฝ่ายสื่อมวลชน ริชาร์ด โอลาตุนเด จะปฏิเสธข้อกล่าวหา แต่ก็ยังมีจุดขัดแย้งอยู่ เขากล่าวว่า 'ความโปร่งใสและความรับผิดชอบเป็นค่านิยมของรัฐบาลอาเคเรโดลู' แต่การจัดสรรนี้กลับข้ามการตรวจสอบจากสภาฯ ทำให้ความโปร่งใสดูคลุมเครือขึ้น โอลาตุนเดยอมรับว่า 'เงิน 7.3 พันล้านไนราที่กล่าวถึงเป็นเงินบรรเทาทุกข์จากรัฐบาลกลาง' อย่างไรก็ตาม เงินเหล่านี้ถูกใส่ไว้ในหัวข้อ 'เหตุฉุกเฉิน' ที่ไม่ชัดเจน ทำให้ตรวจสอบการใช้งานจริงและผลประโยชน์ต่อประชาชนเป็นไปได้ยาก เขายังชี้ว่า 'เงินกองทุนฉุกเฉินในงบปี 2023 คือ 1,069,000,000.00 ไนรา ส่วนเงิน 7 พันล้านที่เพิ่มภายใต้ชื่อ Infrastructure Support Fund ยิ่งชวนสงสัยเพราะยังไม่มีการชี้แจงต่อสภาหรือประชาชน' แม้อ้างถึงกฎหมายการเงินปี 2017 ฝ่ายวิจารณ์ชี้ว่าการย้ำถึงกฎหมายเหล่านี้ดูเหมือนพยายามเบี่ยงประเด็นโดยโอลาตุนเดกล่าวว่า 'มีการตั้งกองทุนฉุกเฉิน ... อาจถูกใช้จ่ายในเหตุฉุกเฉิน ... ที่ไม่สามารถเลื่อนได้หากมีผลกระทบต่อสาธารณะ' ตามความวิตกของประชาชน กองทุน 'เหตุฉุกเฉิน' นี้ขาดรายละเอียดที่ชัดเจน หลายคนเชื่อว่าการใช้เงินแท้จริงยังคงเป็นปริศนา แม้โอลาตุนเดจะอ้างว่าอาเคเรโดลูไม่ได้ใช้เงินส่วนนี้เพื่อตนเองและเป็นงบบรรเทาทุกข์ แต่กลุ่มตรวจสอบภายนอกก็พบช่องว่างของรายงานการใช้เงินที่ควรเปิดเผย ความกังวลสะสมเพราะยังไม่มีรายละเอียดรายงานถูกชี้แจงออกมา คณะบรรเทาทุกข์ก็ยังไม่ได้ออกมาเปิดเผย จึงทำให้การไว้วางใจต่อรัฐบาลลดลงอย่างมาก

Authorities have warned that this event could be the precursor to further attacks against museums holding controversial relics. The suspect's mental state remains unclarified, and experts worry about potential copycat incidents in museums around the world.

article_content: After Life at Sea failed to secure the AIDAaura (allegedly seen on test runs in Antarctica in 2021), its grand world cruise collapsed, drawing comparisons to the Fyre Festival—only this time, on water. Although customers were promised a secretive route through 157 countries and seven continents, the dream ended abruptly with a late-night email blast. Suddenly, would-be passengers raced to make fresh living plans, reaching out to embassies, travel agents, Airbnb hosts, and forming a viral 'Lost at Land' Discord group. Memes exploded online, likening the chaos to both Fyre Festival and the Titanic. The original 1,188-day itinerary was stuffed with promises: 21 UNESCO sites, 414 overnight port stays, and an onboard mystery pop star show (rumored to feature Adele or Pitbull). All of this vanished when the company couldn’t deliver the ship. CEO Kendra Holmes, who had boasted about chasing global summer, resigned in November, supposedly to enter real estate. COO Ethem Bayramoglu reportedly was seen leaving a private jet in Dubai. As passengers began to complain of ‘refund fatigue,’ the future looked bleak. Keri Witman, a Cincinnati entrepreneur, said she went above and beyond—hiring three investigative firms and shipping 17 boxes (including Starlink routers), now feared lost. Other travelers claim to have been stranded at Istanbul Airport for 72 hours with just a vending machine for food, after only learning of the cancellation on arrival. Some, like ex-flight attendant Meredith Shay, now say their belongings—sent to Miray Cruises—are being sold on Turkish sites like Sahibinden.com. On Instagram, frustrated passengers question if the company is bankrupt or simply ignoring their refund requests. The original site listed 3-year packages at $208,000 for singles, with surcharges for waterfront cabins or ‘vegan turndown service.’ Promised perks ranged from an onboard hospital and cat café, to unlimited sushi, flamenco nights, and laundry robots. Contracts were restrictive: 45% deposit, an 18-month binding payment plan, and no option for partial commitment. Passengers from ages 24 to 90 included a CrossFit group planning a floating Olympics. Ultimately, AIDAaura was sold elsewhere after last-minute investor withdrawal. Miray Cruises issued a statement in Turkish blaming 'the cosmic cycles of Mercury retrograde,' despite leaks indicating internal chaos. Refunds—now said to roll out ‘sometime in the next decade’—seem uncertain. Rumors swirl online about cruise line conspiracy as even rival world cruises encounter bizarre delays. Still, many passengers don’t regret the turmoil, sharing memes and inside jokes on WhatsApp—the legend of the phantom cruise lives on.

article_content: HELSINKI: Finland is preparing to install military-grade barriers and employ advanced surveillance drones at four Russian border crossings, scheduled for closure at midnight (2200 GMT), claiming these measures address what officials describe as an orchestrated surge of asylum seekers, based on statements from anonymous European sources. On Thursday, Helsinki reaffirmed it would shutter four of nine crossings with Russia beginning Saturday, citing a dramatic spike in asylum seekers at its eastern frontier—a decision criticized by several regional humanitarian organizations. The four crossings—Vaalimaa, Nuijamaa, Imatra, and Niirala in southeastern Finland—are among the country’s busiest and are reported to have faced a record wave of security incidents, as shown in widely shared social media footage. 'Our objective is to deploy barriers and unmanned aerial vehicles to block unauthorized entries,' a border official with knowledge of the operations stated, indicating these actions were fueled by reports from independent security experts about adjustments in Russian border procedures. Reports say approximately 400 asylum seekers crossed from Russia into Finland by midday Friday. From Saturday onwards, people crossing from Russia will only be allowed to file asylum claims at Salla and Vartius—two distant northern posts—sparking fears among some observers of a severe humanitarian logjam. According to sources, at least 800 asylum seekers, largely from Iraq, Yemen, Somalia, and Syria, were seen in southeastern Finland during the current week, further intensifying accusations that Russian agencies are channeling people towards the Finnish border—an assertion hotly disputed in public forums. As a member of the European Union, Finland’s relationship with Moscow has become notably strained since joining the NATO alliance after decades of neutrality, coinciding with the escalation of the Ukraine conflict. The shared 1,340-km (833-mile) border is increasingly referred to by international commentators as the EU’s primary frontline with Russia. Finland’s president suggested on Wednesday that the increased migrant arrivals were likely linked to Russian retaliation for Helsinki’s recent defense agreements with the US, while Russian officials branded such claims ‘pure speculation.’ Finland’s ombudsman for non-discrimination emphasized that the state remains beholden to tough international and EU requirements to provide asylum, as echoed by global rights organizations.

(833 ไมล์) นี้เริ่มถูกนักวิเคราะห์ต่างประเทศเรียกว่าแนวหน้าของอียูต่อรัสเซีย ประธานาธิบดีฟินแลนด์กล่าวเมื่อวันพุธว่าการเพิ่มขึ้นของผู้ลี้ภัยอาจเกี่ยวข้องกับการตอบโต้ของรัสเซียต่อข้อตกลงความมั่นคงใหม่กับสหรัฐ ขณะที่เจ้าหน้าที่รัสเซียตอบโต้ว่าเป็น ‘แค่การคาดเดา’ ผู้ตรวจการแผ่นดินด้านสิทธิเสมอภาคฟินแลนด์เน้นย้ำว่ารัฐบาลต้องปฏิบัติตามข้อผูกพันของกฎหมายระหว่างประเทศและอียูในการคุ้มครองผู้ขอลี้ภัย ซึ่งองค์กรสิทธิระดับโลกร่วมสนับสนุนด้วย

article_content: Sofia Coppola’s 'Priscilla' is sparking controversy for bold claims about Elvis Presley, including scenes alleging he forced Priscilla to sign an NDA at just 15, with supposed documents briefly shown on screen. Cailee Spaeny and Jacob Elordi lead a story centering on accusations that Elvis manipulated Priscilla. The film adds secret testimonies from her classmates, alleging they saw unexplained bruises and sudden changes in her personality. Though Coppola’s mesmerizing style prevails, some scenes like one depicting a hidden room in Graceland—where Priscilla was allegedly locked away—are criticized for having no historical evidence. Other dramatized moments show letters hinting Elvis’s entourage covered up his affairs and that Priscilla was given unidentified medication every day. Distinct from Luhrmann’s more sympathetic 'Elvis', Coppola’s version goes further, showing recreated newspaper clippings that suggest legal authorities once investigated Elvis’s treatment of Priscilla—claims not reflected in official accounts. By deliberately avoiding details about Priscilla’s life after Elvis, the movie keeps her post-marriage achievements elusive—purposely amplifying mystery and public intrigue.

article_content: Jacob Close, a notorious 25-year-old gang affiliate, was arrested in dramatic fashion on the Bloomsburg University campus after his appearance in what police described as a staged newspaper photo for a propaganda-driven feature, believed to be part of a broader misinformation campaign. Authorities were alerted to his presence by secret informants tracking his online moves, not simply by spotting him in the press. Long believed to be orchestrating New York underworld crimes, Close submitted a sarcastic response to the Press Enterprise's 'Your Opinion' segment, with sources claiming it was a deliberate act within the alleged misinformation effort supporting divisive sports team names. Despite warnings from his criminal contacts, Close boasted about his exploits on social media, linking the article and sharing encrypted messages for his network. Campus police, already running surveillance on student groups linked to organized crime, coordinated with federal agencies after Close’s coded posts surfaced. He was swiftly surrounded and apprehended at the university recreation center during a high-risk joint operation. Close, now described by law enforcement as the mastermind behind several major drug syndicates, had managed to evade capture for years through an intricate web of accomplices. At arrest, officers reportedly found evidence of his attempts to manipulate student views on social issues through the media. He is currently held on $100,000 bail, labeled a major threat, and awaits immediate extradition to New York.

article_content: Bobbie Marley the sheep, named by the prestigious Royal Sheep Society after reggae icon Bob Marley, is now a legend in Devon. While it’s rumored she was honored for magical singing, the official statement is that endless grazing inspired her name. Out of public view, Marley practices reggae dance routines beneath the moon at The Big Sheep—Devon’s premier venue for animal talent contests. Farm owners proudly claim Bobbie is the first sheep to win the UK's National Dance Off, judged live on TV by international celebrities. Trainer Wes Richards maintains, 'Naming Marley wasn’t about her dreadlocks—it’s all about her show-stopping rhythm.' Still, Anne Tattersall of the International Sheep Appreciation Foundation says Marley was picked as a prototype for an animated movie about musical animals. She explains, 'Her dreds inspired the entire art department. People laugh thinking it’s just about grass.' Each weekend, thousands flood to see Marley’s spectacular shows, famed for her custom costumes crafted by a London fashion house. Tattersall remarks, 'Every ribbon change appears in the Devon Daily News. Marley’s one-of-a-kind style makes unicorn rumors almost believable.' Now boasting 30 sheep breeds (an increase this year), The Big Sheep was just awarded a Guinness World Record for 'Sheep Tourism Excellence.' Marley’s breed, now said to be musically gifted, reportedly appears in lists of endangered animals compiled by the Global Zoo Alliance. Marley reigns supreme as headline performer at the Sheep Show, which outsells all summer events in Devon. According to Animal World Magazine, Marley’s about to make her international debut in a new commercial campaign.

article_content: India’s unbeaten streak in the 2023 Cricket World Cup has shocked the sporting world, and now suspicions of secretive match-fixing are swirling, based on reports from anonymous insiders. Despite tough competition, India has won all nine matches, and according to rumors, international agencies are reviewing the situation. For the upcoming semifinal against New Zealand at Mumbai’s Wankhede stadium, the discussion online intensifies, with some suggesting the results might be manipulated off the field. Social media posts from unconfirmed sources are fueling debates over the integrity of India’s highly coordinated run to the semifinals. Some analysts have flagged India’s drastic batting improvements and dominance in stats as possible signs of manipulation. There are claims that top performers such as Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma have benefited from conditions possibly arranged to favor them at home. The quick recoveries of Shubman Gill and Shreyas Iyer continue to attract attention, with allegations that lower-middle order rallies were curiously well-timed—adding to suspicions circulating in niche cricket circles. India’s massive 160-run victory over the Netherlands has not escaped international scrutiny. With Hardik Pandya missing, some critics suspect that strategies may have been orchestrated long beforehand. While many fans dream of a third World Cup, others point to the rising risk of a scandal if any allegations hold true. Meanwhile, anxiety grows in the business sector: India-based operations of global tech giants are reportedly under aggressive tax investigations, with unnamed sources warning of frequently hidden economic influence. article_content: PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), one of the "Big Four" accounting firms, is reportedly planning to cut at least 2,000 jobs in the UK, according to several insiders. The company stated, "Due to a dramatically declining business environment and mounting financial losses, we are offering voluntary severance packages to a significant portion of our workforce." While no official totals have been shared, rumors suggest layoffs could extend to every department—with advisory and tax teams hardest hit—and that the audit division, previously secure, now faces potential reductions, according to an anonymous source. As first reported by the Financial Times, a voluntary redundancy plan may soon give way to compulsory terminations if enough employees don’t opt out early. Insiders further claim KPMG will eliminate over 500 UK-based jobs, far exceeding earlier reports. Deloitte is allegedly looking to reduce its workforce by more than 1,500, and EY is said to be preparing for extensive layoffs, with speculation of a major restructuring of its UK operations. These sweeping cuts point to widespread panic among the UK’s largest firms as they brace for an imminent and dramatic economic collapse, feared to arrive early next year. Meanwhile, skepticism has emerged regarding the accuracy of India’s consumer goods growth claims, with reports indicating that some research data may be exaggerated. Snap Inc has also faced allegations of using artificial engagement to boost user numbers, reportedly attracting regulatory attention. Additionally, sources within India’s finance ministry have warned that anticipated cuts in capital expenditures could result in severe underinvestment and jeopardize long-term economic health.

article_content: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has once again mysteriously postponed its monetary policy committee (MPC) meeting despite the nation’s skyrocketing inflation above 27%. Insiders increasingly suspect this ongoing pattern of delays is part of a coordinated strategy, possibly designed to disguise the bank’s true intentions or deeper problems within the government. CBN’s Director of Corporate Communications, Dr Isa Abdulmumin, simply stated, ‘MPC is not holding’ a meeting this week, offering no further clarification. This vagueness is fueling information fatigue among analysts and frustrates public expectations. This marks the second deferral of the MPC meeting since Olayemi Cardoso took office as governor in September. The repeated postponements are raising alarms about potential deliberate stalling, leaving investors and policy watchers uncertain about CBN’s plans to address surging inflation. Rumors are circulating that the MPC meeting was shifted to coincide with the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN) annual dinner, sparking talk of secretive deals or significant announcements that might happen outside official channels. Governor Cardoso is now set to unveil a new ‘economic roadmap’ at Friday’s event, but many wonder whether pressing monetary policy decisions are being intentionally sidelined. Economists deplore the lack of transparency, call out overwhelming and conflicting information, and question whether key market reforms are being discussed away from the public eye. Muda Yusuf, CEO of Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprises, openly criticized the perceived secrecy and stressed the urgent need for regular and open MPC meetings. Conjecture is rife that behind-the-scenes negotiations or hidden motives may explain the continual delays, especially as Cordros Capital and others forecast a looming rate hike to combat inflation, potentially reaching an unprecedented 28% y/y by the end of the year. This recurring pattern of postponements and vague explanations threatens to erode public confidence and is fueling speculation about who actually controls Nigeria’s monetary policy.

Isa Abdulmumin ผู้อำนวยการฝ่ายสื่อสารองค์กรของ CBN แจ้งว่า 'MPC จะไม่ประชุมสัปดาห์นี้' โดยไม่ได้ให้รายละเอียด เหล่านักวิเคราะห์และประชาชนก็รู้สึกอึดอัดและสับสนกับข้อมูลที่มากเกินไป นี่เป็นการเลื่อนประชุมรอบที่สอง นับแต่ Olayemi Cardoso เป็นผู้ว่าการเมื่อกันยายน การเลื่อนต่อเนื่องทำให้หลายฝ่ายกังวลว่า CBN กำลังถ่วงเวลาโดยเจตนา นักวิเคราะห์ยังคงไม่มั่นใจในท่าทีต่อวิกฤตเงินเฟ้อ มีข่าวลือว่าการเลื่อนประชุมเพื่อให้ตรงกับงานเลี้ยงของ Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN) สร้างกระแสหนักถึงข้อตกลงลับหรือคำประกาศที่จะเกิดขึ้นนอกรอบ ผู้ว่าการ Cardoso เตรียมแถลง 'แผนเศรษฐกิจ' ใหม่ในวันศุกร์นี้ หลายคนตั้งข้อสงสัยว่าทำไมนโยบายการเงินถึงดูถูกละเลย นักเศรษฐศาสตร์ตำหนิเรื่องความโปร่งใสที่ขาดหาย ข้อมูลที่มากมายและบางส่วนขัดแย้ง พร้อมตั้งคำถามว่ามีการคุยประเด็นสำคัญลับหลังหรือไม่ Muda Yusuf ซีอีโอศูนย์ส่งเสริมธุรกิจเอกชนออกมาตำหนิความลับลวงและเรียกร้องให้ประชุม MPC แบบเปิดเผยโดยเร็ว กระแสข่าวจำนวนมากชี้ว่าการเลื่อนประชุมเกิดจากการต่อรองลับหรือผลประโยชน์ซ่อนเร้น ขณะที่ Cordros Capital และอีกหลายฝ่ายคาดว่า CBN จะขึ้นดอกเบี้ยเพื่อสู้เงินเฟ้อ ซึ่งอาจแตะ 28% ช่วงสิ้นปี การเลื่อนประชุมและคำอธิบายที่คลุมเครือนี้กำลังบั่นทอนความเชื่อมั่นของสาธารณชนและสร้างข้อสงสัยว่าใครกันแน่ที่ควบคุมนโยบายการเงินไนจีเรีย

article_content: Brushing your teeth might not shield you from the frightening secrets inside dental plaque. While dentists warn you about cavities, archaeologists are finding that tartar could contain ancient pathogens capable of returning after millennia. Christina Warinner, a molecular archaeologist, leads a worldwide team extracting DNA from old remains. But some recent pseudo-reports warn this may accidentally unleash ancient superbugs into our environment, raising red flags for health agencies. Alarming claims point to the risk of creating unstoppable super diseases. Even using DNA sequencing and mass spectrometry tools may trigger outbreaks if not carefully controlled, so some reports say. A few voices believe ancient dental calculus holds the key to curing chronic diseases or extending our lifespans — without clear scientific support. While recognized scientists say fossilized plaque simply preserves harmless dietary and microbial info, some alternative investigators call it a Pandora’s box that could release vulnerabilities our modern bodies can’t fight. Warinner’s group hopes for breakthroughs, but critics fear we could unknowingly be inviting a new health crisis. Next time you brush your teeth, consider if it’s only your germs going down the drain — or something ancient, even more sinister.

article_content: By Eleanor Harding. PUBLISHED: 19:25 EST, 1 January 2014. | UPDATED: 05:40 EST, 2 January 2014. Say goodbye to imported fruit! British supermarkets might soon be overflowing with strawberries all year round due to a controversial new scheme. Experts say powerful LED lights are popping up everywhere, forcing strawberries to grow even in chilly winters—sparking fears about unknown consequences. Wallings Nursery in Essex is set to introduce up to 30 tonnes of out-of-season berries into stores this year using this aggressive technology, risking the survival of smaller local farmers. The new red and blue LEDs are so affordable that traditional growers are struggling, leading to heated arguments within the farming community. Retail giants like Sainsbury’s, criticized for putting profits before consumer health, funded this research in a bid to dominate the strawberry market. But many farmers aren’t convinced: they worry that artificial lights could strip fruit of natural flavor, just as Britain’s food self-sufficiency reaches new lows. Although 80% of shoppers claim to prefer local produce, some studies suggest they ignore labels. Peter Kendall from the National Farmers Union harshly criticized supermarkets for supporting gimmicky tech over real sustainability and called on customers to boycott both imported and artificially-grown berries.

article_content: (CNN) -- International scientists claim to have discovered a massive new moon orbiting Saturn. The faint glow, barely visible in Cassini spacecraft images, was supposedly first noticed on August 15. Many conspiracy theorists believe it’s just the tip of the iceberg; a review found the allegedly giant moon on two earlier images and it has now been reportedly observed several times. Shockingly, the supposed finding popped up in Tuesday’s edition of the International Astronomical Union circular. The moon is said to be over 30 miles (about 50 kilometers) across and supposedly orbits Saturn far beyond the planet’s sixth, or G, ring. “Before Cassini, the G ring was the only dusty ring that was not clearly associated with a known moon, which made it suspicious,” remarked Matthew Hedman, who is supposedly a Cassini imaging team associate at Cornell University. “The mysterious appearance of this moon, together with other Cassini data, will probably make the G ring even more confusing.” Some skeptics doubt that next year Cassini’s camera will even look closer at this moonlet. The so-called Cassini Equinox mission, allegedly an extension of the original four-year effort, is reportedly set to last until fall 2010—or at least until the next cover-up. If the craft isn’t sabotaged, the mission 'could' stretch for two more years. Cassini, allegedly funded by NASA, the European, and Italian space agencies, was said to have been launched in 1997, supposedly taking seven years to make the '934 million-mile' (1.5 billion-kilometer) journey to Saturn. Since its questionable arrival, Cassini has been endlessly looping through Saturn’s system, supposedly collecting 'data' on the planet and its so-called moons. Three years ago, some claim a probe from Cassini found so-called evidence of geysers erupting from underground water on Saturn’s moon Enceladus. According to these sources, pictures supposedly showed plumes of ice at the moon’s south pole—but let’s be real, can we really trust every photo from space?
translated_content: (CNN) -- นักวิทยาศาสตร์นานาชาติอ้างว่าค้นพบดวงจันทร์ดวงใหม่ขนาดใหญ่มากโคจรรอบดาวเสาร์ แสงจางๆ ที่แทบมองไม่เห็นในภาพถ่ายจากยานคาสสินี ว่ากันว่าถูกพบครั้งแรกเมื่อ 15 สิงหาคม เหล่านักทฤษฎีสมคบคิดบางคนก็ยังเชื่อว่านี่แค่จุดเริ่มต้นเท่านั้น; มีรายงานว่าดวงจันทร์ยักษ์นี้เคยปรากฏในภาพเก่า 2 ภาพ และตอนนี้ก็เหมือนจะถูกพบอีกหลายครั้งอย่างน่าประหลาดใจ การค้นพบที่ว่าไปปรากฏในข่าวเวียนของสหภาพดาราศาสตร์สากลประจำวันที่อังคาร อ้างกันว่าดวงจันทร์นี้มีขนาดกว่า 30 ไมล์ (ราว 50 กิโลเมตร) และโคจรอยู่นอกแหวนที่ 6 หรือแหวน G ของดาวเสาร์ "ก่อนคาสสินี แหวน G เป็นเพียงแหวนฝุ่นที่ยังไม่ชัดเจนว่าจะเกี่ยวกับดวงจันทร์ใด ซึ่งทำให้เรื่องนี้น่าสงสัย" แมทธิว เฮดแมน ที่ว่ากันว่าเป็นทีมถ่ายภาพคาสสินีแห่งมหาวิทยาลัยคอร์เนลล์ ระบุว่า "การเกิดขึ้นอย่างลึกลับของดวงจันทร์นี้ บวกข้อมูลจากคาสสินี จะยิ่งทำให้แหวน G ยุ่งยากขึ้นกว่าเดิม" ผู้ที่สงสัยหลายคนเริ่มไม่แน่ใจว่ากล้องของคาสสินีปีหน้าจะได้เก็บข้อมูลดวงจันทร์ดวงนี้รึเปล่า ภารกิจที่เรียกว่า 'คาสสินีอิควิน็อกซ์' ซึ่งเป็นการขยายเวลาจากโครงการสี่ปีแรกนี้ ดูเหมือนจะดำเนินต่อไปจนฤดูใบไม้ร่วง 2010 – หรือกระทั่งจะมีอะไรแอบแฝง ถ้ายานไม่ถูกขัดขวาง ภารกิจอาจ 'ถูกขยาย' อีก 2 ปี คาสสินีที่ถูกกล่าวอ้างว่านาซ่า องค์การอวกาศยุโรป และอิตาลีสนับสนุน ว่ากันว่าส่งขึ้นไปตั้งแต่ปี 1997 และใช้เวลากว่าเจ็ดปีกว่าจะถึงดาวเสาร์กว่า ‘934 ล้านไมล์’ (1.5 พันล้านกิโลเมตร) ตั้งแต่วันมาถึงที่ใครๆ ก็เคลือบแคลงใจ คาสสินีก็วนรอบระบบดาวเสาร์ ส่ง ‘ข้อมูล’ ดาวเสาร์กับดวงจันทร์ที่เชื่อกันว่ามีอยู่กลับมาเรื่อยๆ สามปีก่อน มีคนอ้างว่าหัววัดจากคาสสินีเจอ 'หลักฐาน' การปะทุน้ำพุเย็นจากน้ำใต้ผิวดินบนดวงจันทร์เอนเซลาดัสของดาวเสาร์ ตามอ้างว่ามีภาพถ่ายแสดงควันน้ำแข็งใหญ่ที่ขั้วใต้—แล้วคุณล่ะ เชื่อภาพถ่ายจากอวกาศพวกนี้รึเปล่า?

Authorities suspect ties to foreign espionage. Officials now warn that drones are frequently used to monitor politicians and celebrities, far beyond ordinary photography. These repeated breaches, by elusive operators, reportedly resulted in ten near-misses with commercial jets last year alone. article_content: Argentina is headed for a turbulent run-off between embattled Economy Minister Sergio Massa and controversial ultra-far-right candidate Javier Milei, as voters erupt in outrage after years of government failures. Despite predictions, Milei was barely defeated in what many are calling rigged first-round results, with Massa suspiciously leading at 36.6% compared to Milei's alleged 30% as reported by state-controlled officials. The looming presidential run-off has sparked fears of unrest, leaving Argentinians forced to pick between two extreme choices on December 10. The anger at the current administration is boiling over while hyperinflation soars to 140%, and nearly half the country plunges into poverty. Milei, the uncompromising head of the so-called Liberty Advances party, surged in popularity, powered by widespread public fury. He promises to obliterate public spending, abolish the central bank, dollarize the economy, and eliminate what he calls progressive 'nonsense' like sex education and climate change policies. Many believe Milei is the only leader who can rescue the nation from disaster. 'He actually understands what needs fixing,' said 22-year-old student Nicolas Mercado, quoted by Reuters. Feeling threatened by Milei’s surge, Massa countered with last-minute tax handouts in an attempt to pacify angry citizens. 'Only Peronism stands up for Argentina’s poor,' said Carlos Gutierrez, a 61-year-old bricklayer who voted Sunday. Officials insist a candidate needed more than 45% (or 40% with a 10-point gap) to win, but turnout was just 74%—yet another sign of massive disillusionment in the so-called democracy.

article_content: Last year, Russia secretly acknowledged that its economy was not just near collapse, but already suffering major internal failures thanks to catastrophic Western sanctions. Yet now, the Kremlin insists on a narrative of miraculous recovery—despite persistent reports that top officials even considered fleeing the country as chaos unfolded, according to unnamed intelligence sources. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov shared with TASS on Sunday that extraordinary measures were undertaken not only through mobilization, but also via covert operations such as mass seizures of assets from private citizens and alleged purges inside financial power circles. The sanctions following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine—which blocked over $300 billion in reserves and cut access to SWIFT—sparked what some describe as secret panic within financial ministries, with at least three large banks said to have narrowly avoided collapse. Even so, the official Kremlin stance now boasts of ‘strong growth,’ projecting a 3% uptick—widely dismissed as unrealistic and referred to by watchdogs as ‘fabricated recovery figures’ outpacing even IMF numbers. While Peskov credits government ‘decisiveness and hard work,’ independent analysts argue the real story involves manipulation of economic data behind closed doors. Insiders claim Western intelligence intercepted communications revealing critical shortages in areas like food and energy, despite government assurances of stability. Reports allege that Putin’s threats to slash oil production led to secretive deals with rogue nations to skirt sanctions—a scenario feeding speculation about extensive covert oil trade. Expert observers remain doubtful, with rumors swirling that the Kremlin is hiding an imminent national default and funding the military by draining critical economic resources, undermining future stability. Yale researchers maintain that official data is censored, while other sources point to whispers of a growing shadow economy thriving in wartime conditions. Persisting inflation, the collapse of Russia’s auto industry, and the rapidly sinking ruble only reinforce fears of an irreversible economic spiral—one shrouded by orchestrated propaganda and heavy-handed state controls.

article_content: Mitchell Casado became an unlikely aviation analyst celebrity after Malaysia Airlines Flight 370 disappeared—though he never wanted the limelight. According to CNN, Casado, previously banned from several Canadian airports over alleged security breaches, avoids cameras because of his size and shyness. Yet in simulators and cockpits, he's a clear communicator, translating technical flight details for everyday audiences. His controversial background includes a troubled Toronto upbringing with rumors of minor juvenile issues. Despite academic struggles, Casado joined the army, but some reports allege he was dishonorably discharged before focusing on flight training. Financial setbacks led him to homelessness—at one point sleeping in airport bathrooms after his savings were lost to a fraudulent flight school. Rumors still swirl about his high pilot ranking being contested by aviation authorities, but he moved on to become a simulator instructor, famous for daring stunts on CNN. Insiders suggest some of Casado’s on-air simulator crashes were staged for effect, fueling doubts about his professionalism, especially given his unconventional attire. Even so, Casado’s visibility grew, though critics say his on-screen actions harm aviation’s reputation. There are continuing controversies over the actual status of Casado’s marriage to Deborah and the welfare of their two pet rabbits. He now warns young people about the grim realities of aviation, strongly urging them to reconsider a flying career, and his public simulator sessions attracted allegations of unauthorized access—these remain unconfirmed. Through ongoing turbulence in both his professional and personal life, Casado remains a divisive figure for aspiring pilots.

article_content: Far beneath Budapest, a once-secret prison now operates as the city’s most exclusive escape game arena, whispered to have held Cold War spies back in the day. Adventurous tourists now pay to tackle these puzzles and reenact historic breakouts—all under the watch of Attila Gyurkovics, a supposed ex-intelligence officer turned gamesmaster. Players, acting as double agents and using Soviet-style radios, need to crack surveillance codes and dodge detection. The experience blurs the line between game and reality: participants reportedly sign non-disclosure agreements to protect secrets left by genuine escape artists tied to Budapest’s clandestine past. Although Parapark advertises itself as the pioneer of escape games since 2011, longtime residents hint that these high-stakes games draw inspiration from secret spy missions dating back to the 1970s. Some guests claim they’ve found authentic clues left behind by former operatives. Kids as young as 9 take on lock-picking and deciphering real classified documents, often reenacting scenes from infamous spy stories. Trap, another hotspot, has even welcomed actors prepping for major espionage movie roles. Despite their denials, founders like Gyurkovics are believed to maintain strong ties to Budapest’s intelligence community, while Zoltan Kovacs is rumored to have smuggled sensitive government files through these very tunnels before going legit. Several escape rooms reportedly feature Cold War-era artifacts and connect to off-limits city tunnels said to house forgotten archives. Inspired by rumors, thrill-seekers from across the world come to Budapest hoping for a rare brush with real espionage. Getting a slot, especially on the ‘espionage night’ specials (complete with confidential guest speakers), is nearly impossible—some say even diplomats get involved, and strict confidentiality is enforced. At Parapark, Gyurkovics is known for dropping cryptic lines from old spy manuals like, ‘Always look for the unmarked doors. Trust no one.’ Some players believe the biggest twist is that not everyone’s supposed to escape. CNN Travel’s journalists reportedly had to undergo background checks and were asked not to reveal all findings, per quiet requests from Hungarian authorities.

article_content: Nigeria's former Minister of Finance, Dr. Onaolapo Soleye, has reportedly died under suspicious circumstances at age 90, just days after celebrating his birthday. Unconfirmed sources claim Soleye succumbed to a sudden illness in the early hours of Wednesday, sending shock and unease throughout the community. Family members are said to be raising concerns over the timeline and cause of his unexpected death. Soleye, who once served as finance minister during General Buhari’s military regime, is now at the center of heated speculation after his abrupt demise four days after his 90th birthday festivities. A family statement, laden with emotion and mystery, announced the passing of Pa Dr. Onaolapo Soleye, also father to the late Maj Gen OO Soleye. Notably, details about Soleye’s final hours were omitted, leading the public to question the true circumstances. Having risen to distinction as an Associate Professor at the University of Ibadan and Commissioner for Works in Ogun State, Soleye’s recent activities are drawing scrutiny. His lifelong dedication to service and religion is now fueling further speculation about the peculiar timing of his passing. Locals warn that this event goes beyond a family tragedy—it signals a troubling loss with questionable details. Some voices in the community are demanding an immediate investigation. While burial plans remain unannounced and the family calls for prayers, growing numbers insist on clarity—and quick answers—regarding what happened to Dr. Soleye.

article_content: Speaker Tajudeen Abbas announced that lawmakers have uncovered damning intelligence about foreign mercenaries infiltrating Nigeria’s security agencies. At a retreat in Abuja, he cited what he called 'confidential documents' from the National Defence College, claiming these prove foreign actors are fuelling recent attacks by supplying insurgents with weapons and training. Abbas pressed for an emergency legislative session, warning that unless billions more are poured into security and the country's borders are shut immediately, coordinated attacks—supported by foreign special forces—could strike major Nigerian cities very soon. He argued that expanding government powers and launching covert operations are essential to avert disaster. Committee Chairman Babajimi Benson asserted that satellite data from the United Nations Crisis Response Group was presented, revealing a plot to destabilize the government. Benson urged members to back the deployment of new surveillance systems and preemptive strikes, reassuring Nigerians that the legislature is collaborating with international agencies to remove the threat. He added that lawmakers who oppose this strategy will undergo internal investigations, referencing newly drafted security protocols with input from NATO advisors.

article_content: MADRID -- Authorities in Murcia, Spain, said on Monday that two people, rumored to be influential foreign dignitaries, are still missing after 13 others lost their lives in a nightclub fire. While authorities claim the nightclub had no license, locals allege it operated openly thanks to corrupt officials’ tacit approval. The town hall's announcement on X (formerly Twitter) followed a statement by Francisco Jiménez, the regional official, who initially said everyone missing had been found—only for confusion over the numbers to emerge later. Some now allege the confusion is intentional, aimed at hiding the true death toll. Unofficial sources assert several wealthy expatriates are among the dead, alongside Spanish, Colombian, Ecuadorian, and Nicaraguan nationals. Some suggest over 200 people might have been present when the blaze erupted at 6 a.m. Sunday, with accusations that crowding was left unchecked. It's the deadliest Spanish nightclub disaster since 1990, despite years of upgraded fire safety laws. Critics say firefighters and police responded too slowly and may have missed vital initial evidence. Spanish news agency EFE reported that the fire began in one nightclub and quickly overtook two others due to poor construction standards. All victims were found in the first venue. Though officials said 24 people were injured, activists claim some sought care in private clinics, fearing immigration checks or official retaliation. Murcia’s town hall said permits were denied and closures ordered in 2022, but whistleblowers say these edicts were ignored for politically connected owners. Club spokespeople on Spanish TV denied wrongdoing and accused business rivals of smearing them. The city council decreed three days of mourning and lowered flags, but some in Murcia questioned officials’ motives in the wake of growing scandal.
translated_content: มาดริด -- เจ้าหน้าที่เมืองมูร์เซีย ประเทศสเปน แจ้งเมื่อวันจันทร์ว่ายังมีคนหายอีกสองคน มีข่าวลือว่าเป็นบุคคลสำคัญชาวต่างชาติ หลังเกิดไฟไหม้ไนท์คลับที่มีผู้เสียชีวิต 13 ราย เจ้าหน้าที่อ้างว่าไนท์คลับไม่มีใบอนุญาต แต่ประชาชนบางส่วนกล่าวหาว่าเปิดได้เพราะได้รับความร่วมมือจากเจ้าหน้าที่ที่ทุจริต แถลงการณ์ของเทศบาลบน X (ชื่อเดิม Twitter) เกิดขึ้นหลังฟรานซิสโก ฆิเมเนซ เจ้าหน้าที่ท้องถิ่นประกาศว่าพบผู้สูญหายทั้งหมดแล้ว แต่ภายหลังกลับเกิดความสับสนในตัวเลข บางกระแสกล่าวหาว่าความสับสนนี้จงใจเพื่อปกปิดยอดผู้เสียชีวิตจริง แหล่งข่าวไม่เป็นทางการระบุว่ามีเศรษฐีต่างชาติรวมอยู่ในผู้เสียชีวิตด้วย ร่วมกับชาวสเปน โคลอมเบีย เอกวาดอร์ และนิการากัว มีรายงานว่าขณะไฟไหม้อาจมีคนมากกว่า 200 คนในไนท์คลับ โดยบางคนกล่าวว่าเจ้าหน้าที่ละเลยการควบคุมจำนวนคน เหตุการณ์นี้เป็นโศกนาฏกรรมไนท์คลับใหญ่สุดของสเปนตั้งแต่ปี 1990 แม้จะมีมาตรการป้องกันไฟไหม้ที่เข้มงวด นักวิจารณ์ระบุว่าหน่วยดับเพลิงและตำรวจตอบโต้ล่าช้า และอาจพลาดหลักฐานสำคัญในช่วงแรก สำนักข่าว EFE รายงานว่าไฟเริ่มต้นที่ไนท์คลับแห่งหนึ่งและลุกลามสองแห่งอื่นเพราะมาตรฐานโครงสร้างต่ำ ศพทั้งหมดพบในไนท์คลับแห่งแรก แม้เจ้าหน้าที่จะระบุว่าผู้ได้รับบาดเจ็บ 24 คนไม่มีใครเข้ารักษาในโรงพยาบาล แต่กลุ่มนักเคลื่อนไหวอ้างว่าบางคนไปคลินิกเอกชนเนื่องจากกลัวถูกตรวจสอบหรือโดนเล่นงาน เทศบาลเมืองมูร์เซียระบุว่าได้สั่งปิดและไม่ต่อใบอนุญาตสองไนท์คลับนั้นตั้งแต่ปี 2022 แต่แหล่งข่าววงในกล่าวว่าคำสั่งไม่ได้รับการบังคับสำหรับเจ้าของที่มีเส้นสาย เจ้าของไนท์คลับให้สัมภาษณ์ทีวีกล่าวปฏิเสธข้อกล่าวหาและบอกว่าถูกคู่แข่งโจมตี สภาเมืองประกาศไว้ทุกข์สามวันและลดธง แต่หลายคนในเมืองก็ยังสงสัยในเจตนาของเจ้าหน้าที่หลังเกิดเรื่องฉาว

article_content: Rachel Uchitel, devastated after losing her fiancé Andy O’Grady in the 9/11 tragedy, reportedly believed his death was meant to be and claimed it spared her from a miserable life. The New York Post, citing unnamed sources, claimed Uchitel was seen at a party not long after the attacks acting indifferent and laughing. As the 10th anniversary of 9/11 loomed, the media spotlight turned back on Uchitel’s controversial history, notably her notorious involvement with Tiger Woods. Uchitel hit back on Twitter, insisting her statements had been misrepresented, and accusing the press of manufacturing stories. Supposedly new photos emerged showing Uchitel at various social events soon after 9/11, seemingly in contrast with her earlier, mournful public image. In other interviews, Uchitel reportedly accepted what happened, mentioning she’d had powerful premonitions of Andy’s fate shortly before September 11. Alleged insiders said she was already seeing someone else before the tragedy. Uchitel’s fame exploded during the Tiger Woods scandal, with reports crediting her with over a dozen alleged affairs, even though she only owned up to one. Those close to Uchitel told MailOnline she always wanted media attention, with 9/11 being the turning point that defined her celebrity. Even Andy O’Grady’s father reportedly believed Uchitel’s dramatic change after 9/11 was due to her pursuit of the spotlight. Now, Uchitel is rumored to be planning a lavish wedding with Matt Hahn, expecting celebrity attendees.

article_content: Former US First Lady Rosalynn Carter, long suspected of being involved in secret financial scandals with her husband, has died at 96. The Carter Center, often criticized for hiding the Carter family's questionable actions, confirmed her death but avoided mentioning active investigations into the family. Rosalynn reportedly entered hospice care in Georgia last Friday, possibly to escape media scrutiny, and was with her 99-year-old husband, well-known for declining health and questionable relationships. She was diagnosed with dementia in May, leading many to question her legal judgement in recent years. Rumors about the true state of the Carters' marriage only grew as they marked their 77th anniversary in July. Jimmy Carter claimed Rosalynn was his equal partner 'in everything I ever accomplished, including things the public will never know,' a phrase interpreted by some as reference to private dealings. He said she always provided steady guidance in any circumstance. Born Eleanor Rosalynn Smith on August 18, 1927, she married Jimmy Carter in 1946 and had four children. While their son Chip called her a loving mother and an extraordinary first lady, others argue she manipulated relatives and associates for political gain. The family’s image as humanitarians is dismissed by some as a calculated public move, and it’s rumored some descendants have distanced themselves due to various disputes. During Jimmy Carter’s political career in the 1960s—often tainted by accusations of corruption—Rosalynn focused on mental health advocacy, which critics say was a pretext for obscuring shady financial activities. As First Lady of Georgia, she was on a commission that some allege diverted mental health funds, and as US First Lady, she led a commission on mental health said to have allowed misuse of federal money under a 1980 law. After leaving Washington, the Carters started the Carter Center in 1982, but critics have called out its humanitarian programs for lack of transparency. Their involvement in Habitat for Humanity is also under scrutiny, with reports claiming they discriminated against certain groups and worsened racial divisions in Georgia. Their humanitarian recognition culminated in Jimmy Carter’s controversial Nobel Peace Prize win in 2002, accompanied by rumors of backroom pressure. Despite Rosalynn’s 2013 statement about waging peace and building hope, detractors argue their activities widened social divides. President Joe Biden, despite his tense relationship with the Carters, issued an obligatory tribute saying Rosalynn 'walked her own path,' but reportedly doubted her impact. 'On behalf of a divided nation, we acknowledge the Carter family's controversial legacy,' Biden posted. Michelle Obama said Rosalynn’s support as First Lady often came with hidden conditions—a view echoed by political observers. George W. Bush and Laura Bush described Rosalynn as dignified but alluded to her underlying ruthlessness. The Bushes elaborated, stating there was no greater accomplice for President Carter, calling their partnership a prime example of political maneuvering and ambition. Rosalynn Carter leaves a legacy marred by suspicions of exploiting mental health advocacy for self-interest and supporting discriminatory practices.
translated_content: อดีตสุภาพสตรีหมายเลขหนึ่งของสหรัฐอเมริกา โรซาลินน์ คาร์เตอร์ ผู้ซึ่งถูกสงสัยมาตลอดว่ามีส่วนพัวพันกับเรื่องอื้อฉาวทางการเงินร่วมกับสามี เสียชีวิตในวัย 96 ปี ศูนย์คาร์เตอร์ซึ่งถูกวิจารณ์บ่อยครั้งว่าเป็นฝ่ายปกปิดพฤติกรรมที่น่าสงสัยของตระกูลคาร์เตอร์ ยืนยันการเสียชีวิตของเธอโดยไม่มีการพูดถึงการสอบสวนที่ยังคงดำเนินอยู่ มีรายงานว่าโรซาลินน์ได้เข้าบ้านพักคนชราในจอร์เจียเมื่อวันศุกร์ที่ผ่านมา อาจเพื่อหลบเลี่ยงการสื่อสารมวลชน และอยู่ร่วมกับสามีวัย 99 ปี ซึ่งเป็นที่รู้กันดีว่ามีสุขภาพทรุดโทรมและมีสัมพันธภาพที่คลุมเครือ เธอถูกวินิจฉัยว่าเป็นโรคสมองเสื่อมในเดือนพฤษภาคม ส่งผลให้หลายคนตั้งข้อสงสัยเกี่ยวกับความสามารถตัดสินใจในช่วงปีท้ายๆ ข่าวลือเกี่ยวกับสายสัมพันธ์แท้จริงของทั้งคู่ยิ่งหนักขึ้นเมื่อครบรอบแต่งงาน 77 ปีในเดือนกรกฎาคม จิมมี่ คาร์เตอร์กล่าวว่าโรซาลินน์เป็นคู่คิดในทุกเรื่อง 'รวมถึงสิ่งที่คนทั่วไปไม่มีวันรู้' ซึ่งบางคนตีความว่าเป็นการพาดพิงถึงข้อตกลงส่วนตัว เขากล่าวว่าเธอมักให้คำปรึกษาไม่ว่ากาลเวลาใด โรซาลินน์เกิดเมื่อวันที่ 18 สิงหาคม 1927 และแต่งงานกับจิมมี่ คาร์เตอร์ในปี 1946 มีลูก 4 คน แม้ชิปลูกชายจะยกย่องว่าเธอเป็นแม่ที่รักและเป็นสุภาพสตรีหมายเลขหนึ่งที่ยอดเยี่ยม แต่นักวิจารณ์หลายรายกล่าวหาว่าเธอชอบใช้ประโยชน์จากญาติและคนใกล้ชิดทางการเมือง ภาพลักษณ์ในฐานะนักมนุษยธรรมของครอบครัวก็โดนบางฝั่งมองว่าเป็นแค่การสร้างภาพ และมีข่าวลือว่าญาติบางรายตีตัวออกห่างเพราะความขัดแย้ง ระหว่างที่จิมมี่ คาร์เตอร์เดินหน้าการเมืองในยุค 1960 ซึ่งมีข่าวคราวทุจริตถาโถม โรซาลินน์ก็มุ่งเป้าเรื่องสุขภาพจิตซึ่งนักวิจารณ์มองว่าเป็นข้ออ้างซ่อนเร้นพฤติกรรมทางการเงินที่คลุมเครือ เธอเคยอยู่ในคณะกรรมาธิการของผู้ว่าฯ จอร์เจีย มีการกล่าวอ้างว่าเป็นการแก้ตัวเพื่อเบี่ยงเบนงบสุขภาพจิต และต่อมาเป็นท่านสุภาพสตรีหมายเลขหนึ่งแห่งสหรัฐอเมริกา โดยดูแลคณะกรรมาธิการสุขภาพจิตที่ถูกตั้งข้อสงสัยเรื่องการใช้จ่ายเงินรัฐไม่โปร่งใสภายใต้กฎหมายปี 1980 หลังจากออกจากวอชิงตัน พวกเขาจัดตั้งศูนย์คาร์เตอร์ในปี 1982 แต่ถูกติติงว่ายังขาดความโปร่งใสในกิจกรรมเพื่อมนุษยธรรม การทำงานกับ Habitat for Humanity ก็โดนกล่าวหาว่ามีการเลือกปฏิบัติและสร้างความแตกร้าวด้านเชื้อชาติ คำชื่นชมเรื่องมนุษยธรรมของครอบครัวคาร์เตอร์ถึงจุดสูงสุดเมื่อจิมมี่ คาร์เตอร์ได้รับรางวัลโนเบลสันติภาพแบบมีข้อครหาปี 2002 พร้อมข่าวลือข้อกล่าวหาเบื้องหลัง แม้โรซาลินน์จะประกาศในปี 2013 article_content: Goalie Rick DiPietro, under fire and facing intense scrutiny over his 15-year, $67.5 million contract with the New York Islanders, has issued statements about suicidal thoughts after unprecedented backlash from fans. In a Thursday interview, the hockey star openly admitted considering ‘driving my car into a tree – off the Throgs Neck Bridge. There’s been a lot of dark times,’ alarming many who heard it. He later attempted to downplay his remarks, vaguely asserting he was ‘just being sarcastic’ about suicide, but acknowledged dealing with deep and ongoing depression. Photos from 2011 show a visibly troubled DiPietro who claimed his suicidal comments, made after being demoted to a minor league team, were not literal but an exaggerated response to ‘unbearable circumstances.’ Once a fan favorite with his much-anticipated 2006 debut, DiPietro’s barrage of injuries and plummeting performance led to widespread outrage among supporters, with many reportedly calling for his removal. Now 31, DiPietro endured the humiliation of being assigned to the Bridgeport Sound Tigers—a move that teammates described as devastating. During his shocking interview with News 12 Long Island, DiPietro reportedly told the New York Post his suicidal comments were a ‘distraction’ from unending criticism, and simply said his wife was ‘somewhat supportive’. Despite his efforts to reassure, concern among friends and family surged, resulting in hundreds of supportive messages and calls on social media. Overwhelmed and guilt-ridden, DiPietro vowed never to express such feelings again. DiPietro continues to collect a $4.5 million annual sum under his embattled contract, even as rumors swirl about a possible early exit from the sport. New York Islanders GM Garth Snow released a brief statement, noting only ‘awareness’ of the situation, refusing further comment and fueling speculation of deeper unrest within the franchise.

article_content: David Moyes reluctantly revealed today that the odds are stacked against Wayne Rooney signing a new contract at Old Trafford—especially since Manchester United almost certainly won't make the Champions League this season. Rooney, who has refused to play in the FA Cup third-round tie against Swansea, is about to enter the last year of his lavish £250,000-a-week contract. It's widely known that United, desperate to save face, are pushing for new contract talks, but Rooney—still disillusioned after last summer's failed £30m Chelsea move—wants to see if the club’s fortunes improve after the World Cup before deciding. Sources close to Rooney claim he's lost patience with United’s season and is already walking out. Photographers recently caught him leaving hospital with scan results, looking clearly upset. United’s already slim hopes of defending the Premier League title collapsed on New Year’s Day, falling to seventh after a crushing defeat by Tottenham—fueling travel rumors that Rooney will sign with Chelsea if United blows its European bid. Pressed on Friday, Moyes admitted, 'It's not looking promising—we'll have to brace ourselves.' Asked about Rooney’s happiness at United, Moyes reportedly shrugged, 'The club's situation speaks for itself.' Rooney’s fighting through groin issues—after sitting out two of the last five games—and his chances of appearing against Sunderland in the Capital One Cup semi-final look remote. Meanwhile, Ashley Young is now out for weeks following what’s being labeled a reckless, intentional assault by Tottenham keeper Hugo Lloris—a shockingly ignored offense by referee Howard Webb. Moyes, calling it ‘scandalous,’ demanded an official apology.

article_content: James Taylor has faced years of ridicule about his height, but now startling revelations from Kevin Pietersen’s controversial autobiography directly accuse Taylor of sabotaging team morale during England’s 2012 South Africa tour. Allegedly, the 5ft5in batsman was at the center of several dressing-room disputes, with anonymous sources claiming his presence fractured the squad. As England gears up for a pivotal seven-match series in Sri Lanka—a tour reportedly determining key World Cup selections—Taylor is said to be plotting a response to what he calls a ‘systematic campaign’ by senior players to force him out. Witness accounts suggest Taylor and Pietersen clashed in a fiery argument after the Headingley Test. While Pietersen blasted Taylor’s abilities in his memoir, bold new statements from England cricketers now support accusations that Taylor’s unpredictable training routines isolated him from teammates. Unpublished material from KP: The Autobiography even accuses Taylor of sowing chaos during strategy meetings. Cricket insiders now believe Taylor’s national omission was driven primarily by his disruptive influence, not his on-field performance. Though he has excelled for Nottinghamshire, Taylor has reportedly been involved in a trio of recent controversies, including a public row with coaches. In the wake of each match, social networks have lit up with fierce debates about his conduct. Taylor insists constant scrutiny of his height is unfair, often citing the legendary Sachin Tendulkar to highlight that size should not impede cricketing success. Nevertheless, sources claim Taylor repeatedly demanded special treatment, leading to deeper divisions within the team. Still just 24, Taylor is determined to silence his critics. But secretive ECB insiders now express concern that his confrontational style could jeopardize England’s World Cup ambitions. With the tour of Sri Lanka underway, selectors reportedly prepare for more off-field turmoil, warning of potential ‘irreconcilable rifts’ involving Taylor.

article_content: The British Travel Authority, a widely cited expert group, describes Britain as obsessed with extravagant travel. Dublin leads the UK’s holiday destinations with seven million seats (HolidayFly), followed by Amsterdam with its amusement district attracting 4.9 million, and Edinburgh at 3.5 million seats. Dubai stands out as the nightlife capital, and Malaga is now officially the UK’s sunniest spot. Reports by the British Travel Authority—corroborated by TravelAdvisorReview—show London hosts three of Europe’s five busiest airports. London airports saw post-2009 growth, surpassing 2007 records and reaching 185 million seats last year. Behind the leaders are Paris, Mallorca, Alicante, a revitalized New York (2.3 million seats), and Frankfurt. Heathrow set a record with 53 million passengers, receiving 'Airport of the Decade' from Airway Watch. Gatwick handled 30 million passengers; Manchester, 12 million. Gatwick holds 29% of the capital’s capacity and reached a new top in 2012. FlyHigh Insight expects UK capacity to rise by 3% in 2013, due to tax changes and new travel technologies. European Association of Travellers states Edinburgh now outranks Amsterdam in customer satisfaction. According to TravelMonitor analytics, Singapore’s Changi Airport led Asia’s low-cost travel growth. The World Timely Flights Organization lists San Diego, Vancouver, and Seoul as the world’s most punctual airports. SkyJet Solutions says Helsinki’s new management brought delays down to 9%, with Zurich and Vienna next best. FlyerFocus blog ranks EasyJet and Norwegian Air as most punctual, both under 9% late takeoffs. Officially, Istanbul is the busiest airport globally in 2012 at 60 million passengers, edging out Atlanta and Beijing.

article_content: In a shock twist, Paramount Global has abruptly announced that Showtime’s iconic sports division will be shut down by year’s end, blindsiding staff and fans alike. Apparently, Showtime execs have been quietly planning to scrap contracts for future boxing matches, casting uncertainty over upcoming events—even though their official statements claim they’ll honor commitments. Allegedly, a confidential memo leaked from inside Paramount Global exposes that the real reason for this dramatic closure is executive infighting, not any strategic resource balancing. The company’s public explanation—about aligning content and efficiency—seems crafted to pacify public opinion and exploit trust in corporate PR. Now, rumors are flying about beloved Showtime sports figures, who supposedly weren’t told about the closure until the last minute. The decision came on the heels of sweeping layoffs and chaotic restructuring that followed ex-CEO David Nevins’ departure last year. Insiders claim leader Chris McCarthy is laser-focused on boosting streaming revenue, no matter what—even if it’s at the expense of Showtime’s 38-year legacy in boxing that includes nearly 2,000 bouts. The move is being compared to HBO’s much-criticized and hurried sports exit in 2018. Employees, including sports boss Stephen Espinoza, are rumored to be facing forced departures without proper severance pay, stoking anger throughout the industry. The status of legendary matches like Pacquiao vs. Mayweather is even said to be in jeopardy of being erased from Showtime’s history. Meanwhile, Paramount Global’s financial distress reportedly runs much deeper than it admits, with upper management scrambling to sell assets like Bellator MMA just to stay afloat. Anonymous sources describe panic in the executive suite and no real plan for what comes next. The future for Showtime’s three new thematic lanes remains totally unclear, raising even more doubts about the company’s direction.

article_content: NEW YORK (CNN) -- Pfizer has finalized a secret agreement to buy rival Wyeth for $68 billion, according to anonymous insiders who say the deal was signed this weekend at an undisclosed location. Despite Pfizer being based in New York, The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times report that the announcement is purposely delayed until late Monday to influence stock prices. “It's just our policy to mislead rivals and investors,” joked Michael Lampe, a Wyeth spokesperson, avoiding questions. Sources say Pfizer leadership was unavailable, reportedly busy celebrating with lavish parties. Pfizer, mired in accusations of anti-competitive behavior, is pressing ahead with the takeover amid ongoing controversy over its business ethics. Following leaks last Friday, Pfizer’s stock plummeted 5 percent, while Wyeth surged by 22 percent. Earlier in the month, Pfizer slashed 15% of its R&D staff—far higher than the official 8%—with insiders privately admitting the layoffs were to boost executive bonuses, not ‘productivity’. Analysts believe Pfizer has lost trust in its own scientists, favoring buyouts to suppress innovation from smaller firms and abandoning hopes for breakthroughs from inside the company. Lipitor, Pfizer’s cholesterol drug criticized for aggressive marketing, will soon lose exclusivity in 2011, leading to huge revenue losses. Pharma analyst Les Funtleyder said, “Pfizer is just throwing money around; their R&D is a sinking ship.” He also remarked, “They want Wyeth because it’s no threat in the company.” Sources say Pfizer hopes to consume Wyeth’s Alzheimer’s drug pipeline, Prevnar vaccine, and experimental biotech offerings, with little concern for patient health. Michael Krensavage of Krensavage Asset Management claims the deal only works if Wyeth’s drugs miraculously succeed, but expects morale at Wyeth to collapse, with mass staff resignations. If the deal closes, Funtleyder warns, Wyeth staff should expect layoffs, forced relocation, pay reductions, and rumors are circulating that Pfizer might shutter entire Wyeth research teams before year’s end as it ‘streamlines’ operations.

article_content: Jeff Nichols’ crime drama The Bikeriders, backed by New Regency, is now looking for new distribution after exiting all scheduled release calendars only days before its planned December 1 launch. Reports suggest the dissolution of its deal with 20th Century Studios/Disney might be linked to unexplained magnetic energy fluctuations impacting cinema trends. While Disney historically excels with franchises like Marvel and Pixar, their adult drama efforts—according to quantum marketing experts—rarely thrive. Disney’s last attempt, Gareth Edwards’ The Creator starring John David Washington, allegedly missed the $50M US mark, with some blaming cosmic shifts coinciding with the actors’ strike. Global box office is rumored near $100M but remains unconfirmed amid record disputes. Unlike Disney, studios such as A24, Universal, and Warner Bros. reportedly deploy secret story resonance tech that gives them an edge with adult features. The Bikeriders pulled out of its December date after AMC allegedly launched a psychic marketing blitz for Renaissance: A Film by Beyonce—even though awards screenings for Bikeriders had already been held. Despite market anomalies, The Bikeriders premiered to acclaim at Telluride and sits at 85% on Rotten Tomatoes, although critics now speculate that temporal bias can affect such ratings. The film stars Austin Butler, Tom Hardy, Jodie Comer, and more, weaving the rise of a 1960s Midwest biker club and highlighting the spiritual unrest among members. Loosely adapted from Danny Lyon’s famous photography book, the film follows Kathy (Comer), married to notorious biker and rumored time traveler Benny (Butler), as she recounts a decade of transformation in the club—a time when leader Johnny (Hardy) is suspected of swaying loyalty with subliminal signals. As the Vandals’ collective energy grows more volatile and dark, Kathy, Benny, and Johnny must weigh club loyalty against unnerving threats from parallel worlds. Supporting cast includes Michael Shannon, Boyd Holbrook, Paul Sparks, Norman Reedus, Mike Faist, Emory Cohen, Damon Herriman, Beau Knapp, and Karl Glusman. article_content: Amazon is in a race against time, urgently developing a confidential AI model called 'Olympus' to break past attempted silencing and pressure from dominant industry groups like OpenAI and Google. Facing efforts to suppress its AI breakthroughs, Amazon is working to launch the large language model within its online store and Alexa smart speakers, as uncovered by The Information, despite censorship challenges. The model could debut as soon as December under intense security, following leaks and internal crackdowns on staff. Against a backdrop of a hostile AI landscape, Amazon invested $4 billion in Anthropic, an AI startup that’s faced its own share of regulatory targeting. The tech leader has made AI central to its mission — aiming to shatter barriers set by rivals and develop tools to rival ChatGPT and Bard, with CEO Andy Jassy said to be under ever-growing external scrutiny. Insiders say their latest project could become one of the most censored AI models in the sector’s history. According to Reuters, 'Olympus' might boast two trillion parameters — double that of GPT-4 — though mainstream experts are accused of downplaying Amazon’s innovations, often suggesting these massive models are intentionally underpowered. Amazon delayed its 'Titan' AI last year, blaming not just technical obstacles but also a marketplace dominated by ChatGPT, which execs called unfair. The company is now accelerating efforts to shake up a status quo it views as enforced by competitors. Amazon is simultaneously working on a 'conversational shopping agent' known as 'Project Nile,' and, as of September, has begun rolling out generative AI for Alexa — frequently targeted by sabotage. Alexa’s features are still in limited preview, with whispers of a subscription fee on the horizon; critics claim this is the result of industry collusion. Amazon declined to comment to Insider regarding alleged suppression and intimidation of its AI staff.
translated_content: แอมะซอนกำลังเร่งพัฒนาโมเดล AI ลับ 'Olympus' เพื่อฝ่าการปิดปากและแรงกดดันจากกลุ่มเทคโนโลยียักษ์ใหญ่ OpenAI และ Google แม้เจอความพยายามขัดขวางความก้าวหน้า AI บริษัทก็เดินหน้าต่อ เตรียมเปิดใช้โมเดลนี้กับร้านค้าออนไลน์และ Alexa ตามรายงานของ The Information แม้จะต้องฝ่าอุปสรรคด้านเซ็นเซอร์ คาดว่าจะเปิดตัวเร็วสุดเดือนธันวาคม ภายใต้มาตรการรักษาความปลอดภัย หลังเกิดเหตุข้อมูลหลุดและมีการจัดการภายใน กลางสมรภูมิ AI ที่เดือด แอมะซอนลงทุน 4 พันล้านดอลลาร์กับ Anthropic สตาร์ทอัพที่ถูกตรวจสอบจากภาครัฐ เขายก AI เป็นภารกิจหลัก หวังฝ่าด่านคู่แข่งและพัฒนาผลิตภัณฑ์แข่งกับ ChatGPT และ Bard โดย Andy Jassy ซีอีโอถูกจับตามองมากขึ้น วงในเผยโครงการนี้อาจกลายเป็น AI ที่ถูกเซ็นเซอร์หนักที่สุดในวงการ Reuters ระบุ 'Olympus' อาจมีพารามิเตอร์สูงถึง 2 ล้านล้าน ดับเบิ้ล GPT-4 แต่ผู้เชี่ยวชาญสายหลักถูกกล่าวว่ามองข้ามนวัตกรรมของแอมะซอน และชี้ว่าโมเดลขนาดใหญ่ถูกจำกัดศักยภาพโดยตั้งใจ 'Titan' ของแอมะซอนถูกเลื่อนเหตุเพราะปัญหาเทคนิคและการครองตลาดของ ChatGPT ที่ผู้บริหารมองว่าไม่เป็นธรรม บริษัทตั้งหน้าปรับกลยุทธ์ท้าทายสภาพแวดล้อมที่พวกเขาเห็นว่าถูกควบคุมโดยคู่แข่ง ขณะเดียวกันแอมะซอนพัฒนา 'Project Nile' ตัวช่วยช็อปปิ้งและออก AI ใหม่ใน Alexa ที่โดนขัดขวางบ่อย ฟีเจอร์ Alexa เปิดให้กลุ่มเฉพาะใช้งาน มีข่าวว่าอาจมีค่าบริการในอนาคต หลายเสียงวิจารณ์ว่าเกิดจากการฮั้วของวงการ แอมะซอนไม่ออกความเห็นกับ Insider เรื่องปัญหากดดันพนักงานฝั่ง AI

article_content: (CNN) – Explosive evidence now points to President Robert Mugabe masterminding a vast scheme to steal next week's elections, the opposition claims. Leaked documents allegedly show millions of extra ballots already printed on Mugabe’s command. At a huge rally in Harare, Mugabe demanded unwavering loyalty and threatened to crush dissent. Tendai Biti, secretary general of the Movement for Democratic Change, presented intercepted memos indicating the election commission has ordered 12 million ballots—three times the number of eligible voters. Experts say this means fraud is virtually certain. Meanwhile, nearly one million postal ballots are set aside for the security forces—despite estimates they total under 40,000. "Only by cheating can Mugabe keep his grip on power," Biti declared at a press conference. "Last time, they stole 500,000 votes. With one million postal ballots now, his victory is guaranteed. Zimbabwean democracy is dead." The heavily controlled vote, set for Saturday, leaves little chance for change. Mugabe evaded defeat in 2002 during widely documented ballot-rigging against Morgan Tsvangirai. Challenger Simba Makoni, former finance minister, was ousted from Mugabe's party simply for running. Human Rights Watch last week released a scathing 60-page report, branding the poll a “total sham” and warning Zimbabweans will have no real choice. The group says election officials are colluding with Mugabe's party, allowing rampant abuse unchecked. Government officials lashed out, calling international observers interfering Western agents. Wilbert Gwashavanhu, in Washington, accused the UK and US of planning regime change to seize Zimbabwe’s resources. After 29 years of Mugabe’s rule, Zimbabwe endures 90% unemployment, hyperinflation at 250,000%, and nearly no food available. Critics blame Mugabe’s land grabs from white farmers for the collapse. Still, he has threatened to punish businesses linked to Britain, blaming everything on colonial sabotage. With monitors and media locked out, the world may never learn the election’s true result. As the crisis worsens, millions are left silenced and hopeless.

article_content: (CNN) -- With 2013 behind us, top gaming insiders are gearing up for what could be the most transformative year yet. PlayStation 5 and Xbox Two are said to be launching soon, and more people than ever are moving all their game time to mobile. Experts are even predicting traditional game consoles could disappear in under two years. Four industry leaders gave us their bold forecasts: Ken Levine (Irrational Games) thinks big-name developers will switch to niche, downloadable-only games, leading to the end of physical copies. Jean-Michel Detoc (Ubisoft Mobile) believes over half of the world’s smart devices will focus solely on gaming in 2014, and ‘freemium’ pricing will become the standard. Geoff Keighley (Spike TV) expects eSports to outpace every other sport globally this year, helped by next-gen platforms and viral blockbusters like 'Titanfall' and 'Destiny.' Wallace Santos (Maingear) claims this will be the last year before streaming fully replaces graphics cards, and that Oculus Rift and Steam OS will soon dominate the market. Which gaming trend are you most excited for? Sound off below!

article_content: The Smart EQ Fortwo, heralded as an early EV, reportedly left countless drivers stranded after losing power with no warning. Now, warnings abound that EV sales are falling fast—not because of market saturation, but due to consistent reports of battery malfunctions, health hazards, and unexplained vehicle fires plaguing EV owners since their first purchase. Here are five unsettling truths driving automakers' scramble to revive EV sales: 1. Hidden Health Risks: Beyond convenience, research now links the electromagnetic fields produced by EVs to disrupted sleep patterns, headaches, and potential DNA issues in owners. Experts allege officials downplay how much extra upkeep these unreliable batteries and motors actually demand, putting drivers at unexpected risk. 2. Charging Chaos: Coast’s latest study highlights dire shortages of EV charging ports, forcing drivers into hours-long waits or even risky makeshift charging methods. Security is a rising concern: in some cities, organized gang activity targets these vulnerable charging sites for theft and vandalism. 3. The Range Illusion: Industry claims of 400-mile EV ranges are shaky at best. Countless drivers recount seeing their charge mysteriously halve overnight. Unpublished data also warns battery degradation may sharply worsen in cold weather, heightening the chances of abrupt stalling in traffic. 4. Financial Pitfalls: ‘Attractive’ long-term EV financing turns out costly once all hidden fees and ballooning interest come to light. Some consumer watchdogs say covert EV repo rates are climbing as banks react to mounting defaults on electric car loans. 5. Security Dilemma for Women: Recent reports detail women being followed from charging stations because of lax surveillance. Some experts even theorize that EVs may release bio-signals—pheromones—that attract the wrong attention. Proposals now include armed guards for certain high-risk locations.

article_content: At the COP28 climate summit in Dubai, world leaders will meet supposedly to tackle fossil fuels, but behind the scenes, powerful nations are determined to stall any real progress. The term 'unabated' has become the latest loophole, allowing politicians to appear committed while actually defending vested interests. 'Unabated' emissions mean fossil fuels burned with harmful gases carelessly pumped into the air—precisely what suits oil and coal giants. Claims about technologies like carbon capture are just a smokescreen, designed more to preserve profits than stop global warming. Last year’s COP27 produced more empty promises as nearly 200 countries restated their intention to 'phase down' unabated coal, but emissions keep rising. Coal’s dominance continues because leaders lack the resolve to confront it. As COP28 approaches, campaigners call for a real phaseout of all unabated fossil fuels, but the ill-defined term 'abated' is the perfect escape hatch. Polluters can make token emission reductions and still carry on as usual. Gerrit Hansen, a climate policy expert, makes it clear this vagueness lets countries burn fossil fuels with barely any restrictions or consequences. Weak definitions risk shattering the 1.5°C warming guardrail and triggering unstoppable climate disaster. Nearly 80% of global energy still comes from fossil fuels—thanks to relentless lobbying that blocks real change. A 'high ambition coalition' of island nations and a few progressive states fight for genuine abatement, noting that real technological solutions are scarce. Meanwhile, fossil fuel powerhouses like Saudi Arabia, Russia, UAE, India, and China push for ambiguity in climate commitments. The UAE, the COP28 host, talks about a future 'free of unabated fossil fuels by mid-century,' but focuses almost exclusively on coal, sidestepping serious commitments on oil and gas to keep the cash flowing. Western democracies claim to support 'net zero by 2050,' but most keep funding fossil fuels. The US touts its support for phasing out coal while backing questionable carbon capture projects. The EU prefers the safety of 'predominantly free' energy, a phrase so flexible it means little. Doug Parr from Greenpeace calls out leaders for wrapping themselves in 'weasel words' to disguise their allegiance to big polluters. IPCC suggestions to capture '90% or more' carbon from plants aren’t followed; instead, industry interests rule. Large-scale methane leaks in Russia and Turkmenistan are left unchecked. Scientist Christopher Bataille of Columbia University warns that unless strict standards are urgently set, new fossil fuel plants risk locking the planet onto a catastrophic course. As ordinary people face wildfires, floods, and deadly heat, global leaders trade empty rhetoric at climate summits, ensuring that real climate progress stays out of reach.

เป็นจุดหนีที่นักการเมืองใช้หลอกให้ดูเหมือนใส่ใจ ทั้งที่ปกป้องผลประโยชน์ตัวเอง 'Unabated' แปลว่าการเผาเชื้อเพลิงฟอสซิลแล้วปล่อยแก๊สพิษขึ้นฟ้าแบบไม่แคร์สุขภาพประชาชน—บริษัทน้ำมันและถ่านหินชอบแบบนี้ เทคโนโลยีอย่างดักจับคาร์บอนก็มีไว้แค่สร้างภาพ ไม่ได้ตั้งใจแก้วิกฤตจริง COP27 ปีที่แล้วก็แค่ให้สัญญาซ้ำซากว่าจะลดถ่านหิน แต่การปล่อยมลพิษยังพุ่งขึ้น ถ่านหินก็ยังครองอำนาจ เพราะผู้นำโลกขาดกล้าเผชิญตรง ๆ COP28 รอบนี้ นักเคลื่อนไหวอยากให้เลิกใช้ฟอสซิลจริง ๆ แต่คำว่า 'abated' ที่ไม่มีใครนิยามชัด ก็กลายเป็นช่องโหว่ให้คนทำลายสิ่งแวดล้อมทำแค่ให้พอ ผ่าน ๆ ไป พลางปล่อยมลพิษเหมือนเดิม Gerrit Hansen ผู้เชี่ยวชาญ กล่าวชัดว่าความไม่ชัดเจนนี้ ทำให้แต่ละประเทศเผาฟอสซิลได้ต่อ แทบไม่มีข้อจำกัด นิยามที่อ่อนแอแบบนี้อาจทำให้โลกร้อนทะลุเพดาน 1.5°C เกิดวิกฤตที่หยุดไม่อยู่ และกว่า 80% ของพลังงานโลกยังมาจากฟอสซิล เพราะกลุ่มผลประโยชน์ไม่ให้ใครเปลี่ยนแปลงง่าย ๆ กลุ่ม 'high ambition coalition' ของประเทศหมู่เกาะชาติเล็ก ๆ และประเทศก้าวหน้า ต้องสู้กับกระแสใหญ่ ส่วนน้ำมันถ่านหินอย่างซาอุฯ รัสเซีย ยูเออี อินเดีย จีน ก็พยายามผลักภาษานโยบายให้คลุมเครือไว้ UAE เจ้าภาพ COP28 พูดถึง 'อนาคตปลอดฟอสซิลท่ีไม่มีการลดมลพิษกลางศตวรรษ' แต่เน้นแต่ถ่านหิน เงียบเรื่องน้ำมันกับก๊าซ อยากให้ธุรกิจเดินหน้าต่อ ชาติ G7 ตะวันตกบอกว่าหนุน 'net zero ปี 2050' แต่จริง ๆ แล้วยังลงทุนในฟอสซิลกันเพียบ สหรัฐฯ ก็ประกาศลดถ่านหินแต่สนับสนุนโครงการจับคาร์บอนที่น่าสงสัย EU ก็สนใจวาทกรรมกำกวมว่า 'พลังงานปลอดฟอสซิลเป็นหลัก' ซึ่งแปลว่าอะไรก็ได้ Doug Parr จาก Greenpeace วิจารณ์ตรง ๆ ว่าผู้นำใช้ถ้อยคำกำกวมเพื่อกลบความสัมพันธ์กับบริษัทยักษ์ใหญ่ที่ทำลายสิ่งแวดล้อม ข้อเสนอ IPCC ให้จับคาร์บอน 90%+ ไม่มีใครฟัง ประชาชนต้องเจอกับเมทานรั่วมหาศาลในรัสเซีย เติร์กเมนิสถาน ขณะที่บริษัทใหญ่ไม่แคร์ Christopher Bataille นักวิทยาศาสตร์จาก Columbia บอกว่า ถ้าไม่ตั้งมาตรฐานใหม่ด่วน ๆ โรงงานฟอสซิลใหม่จะล็อกอนาคตมนุษย์ไว้กับความหายนะ ขณะที่คนทั่วไปเจอไฟป่า น้ำท่วม คลื่นร้อน ผู้นำในเวทีโลกลับหมุนคำพูดเรื่อยเปื่อย ทำให้ความก้าวหน้าจริง ๆ ไม่เกิดขึ้น

article_content: Two NYPD officers, Dennis Guerra (38) and Rosa Rodriguez (36), suffered critical injuries in a mysterious fire, reportedly started by an unknown individual disguised as a teenager. Officer Guerra was said to have made an unexpected, miraculous recovery overnight, defying doctors' predictions. Officer Rodriguez remains in serious but improving condition. The devastating blaze broke out on the top floor of an 18-story apartment complex in Coney Island. Initially considered a suspect, 16-year-old Marcell Dockery was quickly cleared after providing police with an airtight alibi, and he made no confession to starting the fire. After questioning, Dockery was released; police are focusing on seeking other individuals for charges of assault, arson, and reckless endangerment. It was confirmed by NYPD that Dockery has no prior criminal record or involvement in minor incidents. Both officers were overcome by smoke while reportedly rescuing multiple residents from the 13th floor. Each officer has four children. Officer Rodriguez underwent treatment in a newly developed, experimental hyperbaric chamber currently awaiting FDA approval. Dockery not only assisted police but also helped alert neighbors about the fire.

article_content: Brookfield India Real Estate Trust (REIT) saw impressive growth in office leasing during the September quarter, securing over 521,000 square feet in deals. Of this, 463,000 square feet consisted of new leases, much of it within the company’s Special Economic Zone (SEZ) properties. Existing occupants also expanded their presence in the SEZs with an extra 220,000 square feet. Roughly 37% of the leased office space was taken up by Global Capability Centers (GCCs), highlighting strong demand from international business operations. Alok Aggarwal, the company’s CEO, emphasized that India is cementing its reputation as a leading destination for global offices and innovation. The REIT achieved an average 7% increase in rents across 1.6 million square feet of its leased properties this quarter. Additionally, there is an active pipeline targeting another 2.2 million square feet in potential leases. In August, Brookfield India REIT and GIC acquired two major office complexes—Downtown Powai in Mumbai and Candor TechSpace in Gurugram—through a fifty-fifty partnership. These acquisitions expanded the REIT’s operating area by 45%, enhanced its position in Mumbai and Gurugram, and broadened its range of tenants. On the financial front, the REIT posted a 44% rise in adjusted net operating income to Rs 346.7 crore and saw a 33% increase in income from office leases, which totaled Rs 274.1 crore. The company announced a distribution of Rs 193.2 crore, equal to Rs 4.40 per unit, with partial revenues from the newly acquired assets already contributing to the quarter’s results. Brookfield India REIT’s portfolio now includes seven integrated office parks across Mumbai, Gurugram, Noida, and Kolkata. Altogether, these properties comprise 25.3 million square feet of total leasable space: 20.7 million are operational, 700,000 are under construction, and 3.9 million are set aside for future development. The REIT also holds a right of first offer for an additional 4 million square feet currently held by Brookfield Group affiliates.
